rgb: This is an outdoor, stone-paved plaza, bordered at the left/front-left by a tall stone church facade roughly 10 to 25 metres away and, in the far right background, by a colonnaded building more than 50 metres away; vendor carts beneath blue and multicolored umbrellas occupy the steps 3 to 12 metres ahead. Over the 5 frames, the camera wearer lowers their head, changing from an upward view of the church facade in frame 1 to a direct view in frames 2 through 5 of a close circle of about seven people standing 0.5 to 3 metres ahead. A woman in a white top with a head-mounted strap stands directly ahead within the wearer's arm's reach, approximately 0.5 to 0.8 metres away. Immediately to her left, separated from her by 0.4 metres and positioned about 0.8 to 1.0 metre from the camera wearer, is a woman in a blue denim jacket. Both women face away and slightly right relative to the wearer and hold small food cups within their own arm's reach. The white-topped woman's very close foreground position causes her head and torso to partly hide a man in a burgundy jacket about 2 to 2.5 metres ahead beneath the blue umbrella, as well as the lower bodies of those behind her; the foreground women's lower legs are also cut off by the bottom edge. On the right of the woman in white, four men in an olive jacket, black hooded jacket, green shirt-jacket, and maroon sweater form an arc approximately 1.2 to 3 metres from the wearer and 0.5 to 1 metre apart, facing inward toward the group and generally toward the wearer and foreground women. From frames 2 to 5, the wearer moves slightly nearer and pans a little right, the denim-jacketed woman turns her head toward the woman in white, and the far-right man in the maroon sweater, about 1 metre away and holding a cone in frame 4, stays partly cropped by the right edge.
depth: The monocular depth rendering shows an outdoor plaza, with a large church facade extending into the background 8–25 m away above and behind the crowd, and people gathered on paved ground that rises away from the bottom edge. In frame 1, the camera wearer is looking upward, placing people's heads and a blue umbrella near the bottom at approximately 1.5–4 m. Through frames 2 to 5, the viewpoint angles downward and the wearer advances toward two women in the center-left foreground—a woman in a white top and another in a blue denim jacket, both facing away and right—who turn bright white at 0.5–1.0 m. They are within the wearer's arm's reach and under 0.5 m apart. On the right, a semi-circle of four men wearing a dark jacket, black hoodie, green jacket, and maroon top appears in mid-range gray at around 1.5–3.5 m; they face approximately toward the group and partly toward the camera wearer and are separated by 0.5–1.0 m. Farther behind, a burgundy-jacketed man stands 3–4 m away beneath the umbrella, whose canopy is about 1 m above him, while vendor carts on the left lie 8–15 m away. Across all five frames, the foreground woman in white blocks progressively more of the people and umbrella behind her. The maroon-clad person at the far right remains partly clipped by the right border and holds a small object within their own arm's reach. Relative to RGB alone, this map immediately clarifies the continuous ground-plane gradient and metric divisions among the near pair, the mid-ground semi-circle of men, and the retreating church wall. It is nevertheless unreliable for the sky and distant plaza buildings, which reduce to uniform black, and it compresses fine features such as faces and held cups into featureless silhouettes.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view separates individual people, umbrellas, a handbag strap, and a held cup labeled 'bowl' into colored masks, while the unsegmented plaza paving, church, and sky remain black. As the camera angles downward and nears the group from frames 1 to 5, the pink/brown mask belonging to the woman in white, who is 0.5–1.0 m directly ahead and facing away, and the purple/light-blue mask of the denim-jacketed woman, 1.0–1.5 m to the left and facing right, enlarge across the lower center and left. This shows that both women are directly adjacent and within the camera wearer's arm's reach. To the women's right are three to four men, positioned 1.5–3.5 m away and 0.5–1.0 m from one another, who face left and toward the wearer. Behind and above the foreground pair at 3–4 m, a man in burgundy stands below a large blue umbrella; more distant pedestrians and vendor umbrellas on the left are 8–15 m away. The masks track changing occlusion clearly, depicting the foreground women increasingly concealing the burgundy-clad man, the umbrella canopy overhead, and the mid-ground men, while people along the bottom and right borders remain partly outside the image. Compared with RGB alone, the map simplifies counting overlapping people in the crowded scene and identifying small carried or worn objects within the women's arm's reach, including the green cup marked 'bowl' in frame 2 and the diagonal 'handbag' strap in frame 3. Its temporal reliability is poor, however: the cup and strap go undetected in most frames, faraway buildings vanish entirely, and in frame 5 the white-topped woman's hair and cup combine with the person behind her as the labels overlap.
pose: Frames 1 through 4 of the body-and-hand skeleton display are entirely black, with no body or hand keypoints detected despite the plaza crowd standing 0.5–15 m away. A detection appears only in frame 5: one magenta hand skeleton in the upper-left-center area, aligned with the raised left hand of the foreground woman in the white shirt. She is standing about 0.6 m directly ahead of the camera wearer, comfortably within the wearer's arm's reach, with her back facing the wearer and her head turned slightly left. The detected hand lies immediately left of her head and in front of both the denim-jacketed woman roughly 1 m away on the left and the burgundy-clad man approximately 3 m behind. Its fingers curl around the small green cup, which is within the white-shirted woman's own arm's reach, while her torso obscures the people at her rear. In frame 5, the magenta wireframe reveals the precise finger articulation and the direction of the grip around the cup more clearly than the motion-blurred RGB view by itself. Even so, the map is overwhelmingly undependable for determining spatial arrangement, distance, facing, or tracking multiple people: it detects none of the yellow body skeletons in any of the five frames and misses all the other visible hands carrying food or cups throughout frames 2 to 5.
